levels.name: Street, 42nd St at Vanderbilt Ave
levels.note: The model's street level. 42nd St falls about 3.4 m to Lexington Ave and about 8 m to 3rd Ave (NYC ground heights); the model keeps the street flat, so the machines that reach the street east of here look longer than they are.

levels.name: One Vanderbilt mezzanine (B1)
levels.note: The elevator list calls this the SUMMIT, subway and Grand Central Terminal level. Its depth is this app's usual one storey below the street: assumed. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

levels.name: Mezzanine and Shuttle platform level (B2)
levels.note: 18 ft (official escalator rise) below the street at Park and Lexington, plus 3.4 m for the fall of 42nd St between there and Vanderbilt Ave. Wikipedia gives the Shuttle as about 20 ft (6.1 m) deep; it is drawn on this level because the passage joins them without a machine. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

levels.name: 4 5 6 platforms
levels.note: Depth assumed, the deepest that clears the western mezzanine for the 7 below it, whose depth is official: tracks 1.2 m below the platform and 2.3 m of headroom under them. Trains still fit under the main mezzanine. The elevators that reach this level have no rise in the MTA's list, and Wikipedia's about 50 ft looks too deep beside the rises that are listed. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

levels.name: Western mezzanine above the 7
levels.note: 19 ft 7 7/8 in below the main mezzanine (official escalator rise). Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

levels.name: LIRR Madison Concourse
levels.note: Long Island Rail Road, not the subway. About 50 ft below the street on KPF's section. The Shuttle's escalators reach it. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

levels.name: Central and eastern mezzanines above the 7
levels.note: 40 ft below the main mezzanine (official escalator rise). The eastern one is put at the same depth: its escalators' 50 ft rise, from a street about 8 m lower, gives within about 2.4 m of this. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

levels.name: 7 platform
levels.note: 51 ft 4 in below the main mezzanine (official elevator rise), which the two escalators on the way down add up to within 2 in. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

levels.name: LIRR upper platforms
levels.note: Long Island Rail Road, not the subway. About 120 ft on KPF's section; Wikipedia's other page gives the upper level as about 130 ft. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

levels.name: LIRR mezzanine
levels.note: Long Island Rail Road, not the subway. About 137 ft on KPF's section; a secondary source says more than 140 ft below Park Ave. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

levels.name: LIRR lower platforms
levels.note: Long Island Rail Road, not the subway. About 155 ft on KPF's section; Wikipedia's other page gives the lower level as about 150 ft. Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.

known_issues.text: Rises come from the MTA's machine list. Its escalators on the way to the 7 add up to 51 ft 6 in; its elevator lists 51 ft 4 in. The 4 5 6 platforms' own depth is not listed and is assumed.

KPF's section and axonometric show twin caverns under a long escalator, and the axonometric labels them subway. They are Grand Central Madison, the Long Island Rail Road's station, so they are drawn here apart from the subway, in their own colour. They are built from KPF's section and secondary sources, and no public plan gives their walls.
Several machines share a listed position, and some are far from where they must be: ES210 is about 50 m off, ES608X and ES609X are about 165 m from the corner they name, and ES610X has none.
EL296 is listed as a street elevator, but the MTA's entrance list has no step-free street entrance near it. Not resolved.
The outline marks the area that holds the station, not its walls. It may include rooms the public cannot reach.
Only public circulation is modelled. Staff rooms, plant rooms, emergency exits and other non-public spaces are left out on purpose. Street stairs that have no machine are not drawn.

Opening and landing construction is illustrative: 0.65 m end plates, 2.5 m opening headroom, guard profiles and door thresholds are not surveyed dimensions. Existing source tiers and equipment endpoints are retained.
